why: NOTES-FROM-PLANNING.md entry 217 section 3. GitHub caps none of these for release assets, but the project keeps itself to a budget so it stays a reasonable use of a free service. Alan changes a number here and nowhere else.

grouplab releases, the builds.why: about thirty nightlies of five packages near 470 MB each, which the thirty release rule already keeps to, with room for the stable releases

grouplab releases, test-data.why: the large samples CI fetches; today two scans near 60 MB, so this is room for about thirty more

grouplab Actions artifacts.why: build and test output kept for days, not months; retention is set short so this is rarely reached

grouplab Actions caches.why: GitHub's own cap for one repository's caches, which it enforces by evicting the oldest

grouplab-crash-reports.why: issues are text; a gigabyte is far more than a project this size writes

grouplab-submissions-archive releases.why: submissions of 3 to 60 MB each, so between four hundred and eight thousand of them; entry 217's own example

grouplab-testdata.why: the public test data repository; its large files live on the test-data release instead

grouplab-backups releases.why: entry 222: seventeen nightly backups kept at about 450 MB each, with room for the repository and the originals to grow
